subject.name_or_desc: A gentleman (the querent) seeking an office or place of preferment

context.question: If he should obtain the office or place he looked after (if attain the preferment desired)?
context.asked_at: The same time, within four or five minutes, as the preceding figure; no separate date is stated.
context.setting: The figure was erected at the same time, within four or five minutes, as the preceding figure (the King's Irish forces and the Queen's advance). He employed as his friend a solar man.

attachments.key_positions: The Ascendant and Venus for the querent; the tenth house for the office or place of preferment; the Moon placed in the tenth, applying to a trine of Saturn, who hath exaltation in the Ascendant, receives Venus and is received of her again; Saturn also lord of the fourth; the Sun in the seventh house in opposition to the Ascendant and with the Dragon's Tail, he being lord of the eleventh (the pretended friend); the Moon separating from a square of Mercury
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, Chap. LXXXVI: if attain the preferment desired (Fig. 28 in the 1852 Zadkiel edition)
provenance.version: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR, auxiliary/christian-astrology-vol1-3_djvu.txt); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition (Introduction to Astrology) and the second OCR (christian-astrology-1647-original_djvu.txt) where noted
